correctness.rationale: All constraints and support extrema are reconstructed using explicit feasible points; the reflection-containment halfspace identity is algebraically necessary and sufficient. Summing m-1 prefix gaps and coordinate floors proves the sharp lower bound. A closed-form center saturates it. Tight-prefix equalities have independent rank in triangular coordinates; an explicit epsilon witness gives all remaining inequalities strict. Exact rational active-set verification passes 10 cases with 210 vertices and 2376 reflected-vertex/inequality comparisons. Positive increments and the multichain range m>=2 are explicit; finite enumeration is not miscast as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Direct comparison of claims found no published calculation of the affine reflection asymmetry or full center locus for the genuinely multicolumn straight-shape generalized Pitman–Stanley polytope. The original multichain primary text determines vertices, faces and flow realization; it does not state this theorem. Distinct invariant/parameter comparisons exclude a known one-column density result and the Euclidean-inradius calculation from logically covering the m>=2 theorem. A broader marked-order theorem under different terminology remains a bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: Equivalent descriptions of these flow polytopes as marked order/flow polytopes may admit unlocated general reflection-asymmetry formulas.
The original family with one dominance column is excluded from the novelty claim and may be inferred from broader polymatroid-density results.
A bounded literature comparison does not independently certify priority against all publications or unpublished research.

value.rationale: The generalized Pitman–Stanley flow-polytope family has substantive independent combinatorial study and a natural reflection-asymmetry question. The exact additive multichain law and full center polytope, especially the maximizing-prefix dimension phase diagram, answer it for all positive weights rather than one arbitrary finite slice. Same-asymmetry/different-center-dimension examples supply qualitative structure; no broader theorem is claimed.
